title: When Agents Talk, Secrets Travel: Topology-Driven Leakage and Recipient-Conditioned Sanitization in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
abstract: arXiv:2610.16039v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Multi-agent LLM systems (MALS) introduce a privacy-leakage problem that conventional sensitivity-based defenses miss, since information disclosed to one authorized agent can propagate through routine coordination to an unauthorized one, without compromise or malicious behavior. This motivates topology-aware enforcement that blocks unauthorized propagation while preserving authorized disclosure. We evaluate 485 scenarios across coordinator-worker, peer-to-peer, and hierarchical topologies, instrumenting seven communication channels and measuring surface leakage and disclosure to topology-introduced recipients. We introduce RECONS, a Detect -> Decide -> Transform sanitizer conditioning intervention on recipient and execution context rather than sensitivity alone. Topology changes where protected information propagates, with disclosure to topology-introduced recipients rising from 0% to 52.2% while surface leakage stays nearly flat at 60.

translated_title: 当智能体对话时，秘密随之传播：多智能体LLM系统中的拓扑驱动泄露与基于接收者的净化机制
translated_abstract: 多智能体LLM系统（MALS）引入了一种传统基于敏感度的防御措施无法察觉的隐私泄露问题：披露给某个授权智能体的信息可以通过常规协作传播给未授权的智能体，而全程无需任何系统被攻破或存在恶意行为。这促使我们需要拓扑感知的执行机制，在阻断未授权传播的同时保留授权披露。我们在协调者-工作者、点对点和分层三种拓扑结构下评估了485个场景，对七个通信通道进行监测，并测量表面泄露以及向拓扑引入的接收者的信息披露情况。我们提出了RECONS，一个“检测→决策→转换”的净化器，其干预策略基于接收者和执行上下文进行条件判断，而不仅仅依赖敏感度。拓扑结构会改变受保护信息传播的路径，向拓扑引入的接收者的信息披露率从0%上升至52.2%，而表面泄露率则几乎保持在60%不变。
tldr: 多智能体LLM系统中信息会经拓扑结构向未授权接收者扩散（披露率从0%升至52.2%），论文提出基于接收者与执行上下文进行“检测-决策-转换”的RECONS净化器，在保留授权披露的同时阻断未授权传播。
en_tdlr: In multi-agent LLM systems, secrets propagate through topology to unauthorized recipients (disclosure rising from 0% to 52.2%); the paper proposes RECONS, a Detect→Decide→Transform sanitizer conditioned on recipient and execution context rather than sensitivity alone, blocking unauthorized propagation while preserving authorized disclosure.
